_comments: Payment terms — the lookup the due-date walk resolves against (D83).
THIS TABLE WAS EMPTY, and that was not a cosmetic gap. `OrderHeader.DueDate` is what the aging
report ages, what `Orders.GetOverdueWorklist` filters on, and what an invoice prints. With no
terms to resolve and nothing deriving a date, the column was null on every order and the
collections worklist returned zero rows against 67 orders carrying an unpaid balance — a screen
reporting a quiet afternoon because its only input never existed.
NetDays is the whole of the arithmetic: DueDate = OrderDate + NetDays. `DueOnReceipt` is 0 and is
the terminal rung of the walk, so every order gets a real date rather than a null.

fields.Name: Due on Receipt
fields.Description: Payable when the invoice arrives. The terminal default of the terms walk (D83) — an order that resolves to nothing lands here rather than on a null due date.
